Terms.subtitle: These terms govern the use of this website and of the private areas reached from it. Contracted services are governed by their own contract.

toc.label: 2. What you will find on this site

aceptacion.title: 1. Purpose and acceptance
aceptacion.p1: These terms govern the use of this website and of the private areas reached from it: the client area for communities, buildings and companies, and the resident app. The website belongs to the company identified at the end of this document.
aceptacion.p2: What they do not govern is the delivery of the services themselves. Concierge, security, cleaning, gardening, pool and general maintenance services are governed by the contract signed with each community, building or company, and that contract prevails over this text. By browsing the site or using any of its features you accept these terms; if you do not agree, please do not use them.

servicios.title: 2. What you will find on this site
servicios.intro: This site is informational and, for existing clients, a management tool. From here you can:

list.rest: concierge, security, cleaning, gardening, pools and maintenance, and the areas we cover.
the contact form starts a commercial conversation. Sending it does not contract anything or bind either party.
for communities, property managers and companies with a contracted service. It holds incidents, quotes, invoices and service details.
for people living in a community with a contracted service: report an incident, follow its answer and read the noticeboard.
browse published openings and send an application.
general articles about building maintenance and community management. They are guidance only and replace neither a technical report nor professional advice.

servicios.outro: We may change, extend or withdraw any of these sections. That affects the website, never a service already contracted: what has been agreed in a contract is delivered even if the site changes.

cuenta.title: 3. Access to the client area
list1: There is no open sign-up: accounts are created by us for the client, for the property manager they appoint, or by invitation for residents of a community with a contracted service.
The contact details you give us must be accurate and kept up to date: they are how we reach you about an incident or a visit.
Credentials are personal and must not be shared. If several people in the management office need access, request an account for each.
You are responsible for what is done from your account while it is open.
Tell us as soon as you suspect someone has accessed it without your permission, so we can close that session.
cuenta.securityText: We apply security measures that are reasonable and proportionate to the data involved. On your side, use a password unique to this service and sign out on shared devices. The client area itself lets you see open sessions and close them.

uso_aceptable.title: 4. Acceptable use
uso_aceptable.intro: When using this site and the client area, you agree not to do any of the following:
list: Access or try to access information about communities, units or people that is not yours to see.
Use the data shown in the client area —residents, homes, incidents, access logs— for anything other than managing the contracted service.
Extract the site's content in bulk or by automated means without our authorisation.
Interfere with the operation of the site, the app or the systems behind them.
Introduce harmful software or code.
Impersonate another person, community or company, or misrepresent your relationship with them.
uso_aceptable.warning: If this happens we may suspend access immediately to protect everyone else, and report the conduct where it warrants it. The service's contractual relationship is a separate matter and follows its own contract.

propiedad.title: 5. Intellectual property
propiedad.p1: The texts, images, brand, site design and the software behind the client area and the resident app belong to the company or to those who licensed them to us, and are protected by intellectual and industrial property law.
propiedad.p2: What you upload remains yours: the photos of an incident, the documents you attach or the CV in an application. By sending it you authorise us to use it only for what it was sent for —resolving that incident, handling that request or assessing that application— and for the period explained in the privacy policy.
propiedad.sub3: What you may do with our content
propiedad.p3: You may read and print the site's content for personal use or to manage your community. Reproducing, distributing or modifying it for commercial purposes requires our written authorisation.

pagos.title: 6. Contracting and invoicing
list: The price of each service is agreed by contract before we start delivering it, following the fixed quote we prepared for your community, building or business.
What is contracted, its scope and its term are set out in that contract. This website is not where services are contracted and does not replace what was signed.
Invoices for contracted services are available in the client area.
Payment is made as agreed in the contract (transfer, direct debit or another agreed method), not through a payment gateway on this website.
Any claim about an invoice can be raised through the usual contact channels or from the client area.

privacidad.title: 7. Privacy
privacidad.text: Your privacy is important to us. Please review our
privacidad.textAfter: to understand how we collect, use and protect your personal information.

garantias.title: 8. Warranties and liability
garantias.intro: What follows refers to this website, not to the services we deliver. Contracted services answer for what their contract and the law require, and nothing in this section limits that:
list: The site's informational content is guidance: it may contain errors or become outdated, and replaces neither a technical report nor professional advice.
We aim to keep the site and the client area available at all times, but we cannot guarantee there will be no interruptions for maintenance or reasons beyond our control.
We are not responsible for the content of third-party sites we link to.
None of the above affects the rights that consumer law grants to anyone holding that status.

terminacion.title: 9. Suspension and end of access
terminacion.p1: We may suspend access to the client area if we detect any of the misuse described above or a risk to data security. Unless urgency prevents it, we give notice first.
terminacion.p2: Access ends when the contractual relationship with the community, building or company ends. From then on, data is kept or deleted as explained in the privacy policy, not as stated in this document.
terminacion.p3: Clauses that by their nature must survive the end of access —liability, intellectual property and governing law— continue to apply.

ley.title: 10. Governing law
ley.p1: These terms are governed by Spanish law.
ley.p2: For any dispute, the parties submit to the courts that have jurisdiction under the law. Where the user is a consumer, the court of their domicile has jurisdiction, as consumer law provides.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.subtitle: How we handle the personal data of anyone who visits this site, writes through the contact form, applies for a job, uses the whistleblowing channel or signs in to the private area.

toc.label: 3. What we use it for, and on what legal basis

responsable.title: 1. Who processes your data
responsable.intro: The data controller — who decides why and how your data is used — is:
responsable.dpo: Questions about this policy and requests to exercise your rights are handled at the email address above. If a Data Protection Officer is appointed at any point, their contact details will be published here and notified to the Spanish Data Protection Agency.

recopilacion.title: 2. Data we collect
recopilacion.intro: We collect what you give us in each form and what your use of the site generates. Nothing else: we do not buy lists and we do not obtain your data from third-party sources.

list1.rest: name, name of the community or company, email and/or phone, and the message you write. If you answer them — they are optional — also the qualifying questions: profile (community, property manager or company), service you are interested in, area, expected timeframe and number of properties you manage.
if you tick that box, your consent to receive commercial information about our services. It is a separate box of its own.

if you accepted analytics cookies in the cookie notice, the campaign parameters of the address you arrived from (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, gclid, fbclid), the landing page and the site that linked to us. If you did not accept them, they are neither collected nor sent.
first and last name, email, phone, town, cover letter, LinkedIn profile if you provide one, and your CV as a PDF. We do not ask for a photograph, date of birth, nationality or ID number.
the facts you report and, if you choose to identify yourself, your name and email. You may file the report anonymously.
your account details (name, email, community or building managed) and the quotes, invoices and incidents linked to your contract.
your account, the unit you occupy in the community and the incidents you report through it.

list2.rest: pages visited, time spent and actions taken, only if you accept analytics cookies.
device type, operating system and browser.
country and region inferred from your IP address, so we know which areas potential clients visit us from. It is not your exact location and it does not come from GPS.

when you submit any public form, Cloudflare Turnstile receives your IP address and technical browser data in order to tell people apart from automated submissions. It is essential for the form to work.

pages that show a map request the imagery from an external provider (Esri), which receives your IP address when serving it. It happens as soon as the map is drawn, it is part of displaying the page and it sets no cookies.

uso.title: 3. What we use it for, and on what legal basis
uso.intro: Each purpose has its own legal basis and its own retention period. This is the full list:

rows.purpose: Answering your quote request or enquiry and preparing a proposal.
rows.retention: 1 year from the last contact, unless the enquiry leads to a contract.

rows.purpose: Sending you marketing communications about our services.
rows.basis: Your express consent, in a separate box: art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and art. 21 LSSI.
rows.retention: Until you unsubscribe, from the link in every email.

rows.purpose: Recording where the enquiry came from (campaign, referrer) to see which channels work.
rows.basis: Your consent, given by accepting analytics cookies: art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and art. 22.2 LSSI.
rows.retention: The same as the enquiry it belongs to.

rows.purpose: Assessing your application in a recruitment process.
rows.basis: Pre-contractual steps at your request, art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
rows.retention: The CV, 6 months; the rest of the application, 1 year.

rows.purpose: Keeping your application for future openings (talent pool).
rows.retention: 12 months from the moment you give it.

rows.purpose: Handling a report filed through the whistleblowing channel.
rows.basis: Legal obligation, art. 6(1)(c) GDPR and Spanish Act 2/2023.
rows.retention: 3 months from receipt if no investigation is opened; if one is, for as long as it lasts and as long as needed to document it.

rows.purpose: Providing and managing the contracted service and giving you access to the private area.
rows.basis: Performance of the contract, art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
rows.retention: For the duration of the contract and, afterwards, the applicable limitation periods.

rows.purpose: Meeting accounting, tax and invoicing obligations.
rows.retention: 6 years under the Spanish Commercial Code and 4 under the General Tax Act, from the close of the financial year.

rows.purpose: Logging access and operations so a security incident can be investigated.
rows.basis: Our legitimate interest in protecting the platform and the data in our custody, art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
rows.retention: Audit log 1 year; private-area access log 6 months; inactive sessions 30 days.

rows.purpose: Measuring site usage in aggregate in order to improve it.
rows.basis: Your consent in the banner, art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and art. 22.2 LSSI.
rows.retention: As stated in the cookie policy.

rows.basis: Our legitimate interest in protecting ourselves from spam and abuse, art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.

uso.obligationLabel: Do you have to give us this data?
uso.obligation: The fields marked with an asterisk are the ones we need for what you are asking: without them we cannot answer your enquiry or process your application. The rest are optional and leaving them blank has no consequence.
uso.automated: We do not take automated decisions and we do not build profiles that produce legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affect you. Decisions about your enquiry, your application or your incident are taken by a person.
uso.highlight: Where the basis is your consent you can withdraw it at any time by writing to our data protection address or, for cookies, from the preferences panel. Withdrawing is as easy as giving it and does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out beforehand.

compartir.title: 4. Who we share it with
compartir.intro: We do not sell or rent your personal data. The following have access to it, solely in order to provide us with their service and under a processor agreement signed in accordance with art. 28 GDPR:

list.rest: whoever hosts the site, the private area and the database.
the service that sends out notices, confirmations and marketing messages.
where attached documents, incident photos and CVs are kept.
Google, only if you accept analytics cookies.
Cloudflare, which verifies that whoever submits a form is a person.

list.strong: Field staff assigned to your service:
list.rest: if you are a client, the Imora staff — concierge, maintenance, cleaning or other — who need your contact details or your community's in order to deliver the contracted service.
the tax agency, social security, law enforcement and the courts, where a legal rule requires us to provide the data.

compartir.outro: The map provider (Esri) is not a processor: it is a third party that receives your IP address when serving the map imagery, like any server the browser requests a file from. Beyond the above there is no disclosure of data. Should there be one in future, it will be announced on this page before it happens.

transferencias.title: 5. International transfers
transferencias.intro: Some of the providers above are located in the United States, so part of the processing involves an international transfer. These are the transfers there are, and the safeguard for each:

list.rest: only if you accept analytics cookies. Google LLC is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, which the European Commission found to provide an adequate level of protection by decision of 10 July 2023, and standard contractual clauses are in place as an additional safeguard.
receives your IP address and technical browser data when you submit a form. Cloudflare, Inc. is certified under the same Data Privacy Framework and has standard contractual clauses in place.
receives your IP address when serving the map imagery on pages that show a map. The transfer relies on standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.

transferencias.outro: Beyond these cases we do not transfer personal data outside the European Economic Area. You can ask us for a copy of the safeguards in place by writing to our data protection address.

retencion.title: 6. How long we keep it
retencion.p1: The retention period for each purpose is in the table in section 3. As a general rule we keep data for as long as the purpose it was collected for lasts and, after that, blocked for the limitation periods of any liabilities that may arise — four years for tax matters, six for commercial matters and whatever applies in employment matters — available only on request from judges, courts or public authorities.
retencion.p2: Once those periods have passed we delete the data or anonymise it so that you can no longer be identified from it.

derechos.title: 7. Your rights
derechos.intro: You may exercise the following rights over your personal data, free of charge:

list.rest: find out what data of yours we process and get a copy.
correct inaccurate data or complete what is missing.
ask us to delete it once it is no longer needed (the “right to be forgotten”).
ask us to keep the data but stop using it while a challenge or an objection is resolved.
receive the data you gave us in a structured, commonly used format, or have us send it to another controller.
object to processing based on our legitimate interest, and in any case to marketing communications.
withdraw at any time any consent you have given, without that affecting the lawfulness of earlier processing.

derechos.outro: To exercise any of them write to us at
derechos.outroEnd: stating which right you are exercising. We may ask you to prove your identity if we have reasonable doubts about who is making the request.
derechos.deadline: one month from receipt of your request. If it is particularly complex, or several requests pile up, that period may be extended by two further months, and we will tell you within the first month and explain why.
derechos.complaintLabel: Lodging a complaint with the supervisory authority:
derechos.complaint: if you believe we have not handled your request properly, or that we are processing your data improperly, you may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (C/ Jorge Juan 6, 28001 Madrid). You do not have to complain to us first, although we would like the chance to sort it out.

menores.title: 8. Minors
menores.p1: This site is not aimed at minors. In Spain, from the age of fourteen a person may consent to the processing of their data on their own (art. 7 of the Spanish Data Protection Act); below that age the consent of whoever holds parental authority or guardianship is required.
menores.p2: Even so, the contact form asks you to declare that you are of legal age: what is requested there is a service contracted for a community, a building or a company, and there is no sense in processing it with a minor. If we find that we have received a minor's data without the necessary consent, we delete it as soon as we know.

cookies.title: 9. Cookies
cookies.text: We use cookies and similar technologies. See our
cookies.textAfter: for details of which ones we use, how long they last and how to accept them, reject them or change your mind later.

seguridad.title: 10. Security
seguridad.intro: We apply technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, in line with art. 32 GDPR:
list: SSL/TLS encryption on all communications with the site and the private area.
Passwords are not stored: what is kept is a cryptographic hash that cannot be reversed.
Two-step verification available on internal access.
Role-based access: each person sees what they need for their job and nothing more.
A log of who consults or changes what, so an incident can be reconstructed.
Antivirus scanning of every uploaded file before it is stored.
Regular backups and restore testing.
seguridad.breach: we keep an internal register of security breaches. If one of them poses a risk to your rights, we notify the Spanish Data Protection Agency within the 72 hours required by art. 33 GDPR and, where the risk is high, we tell you as well.

Cookies.title: Cookies Policy
Cookies.subtitle: We use cookies and similar technologies to improve your experience. Here we explain what they are, how we use them and how you can manage them.

que_son.title: 1. What are cookies?
que_son.p1: Cookies are small text files that websites place on your device when you visit them. They are used to make websites work more efficiently.
que_son.p2: Cookies allow the website to remember your actions and preferences so you don't have to re-enter them every time you return.
que_son.highlight: Art. 22.2 of the Spanish LSSI-CE — the national transposition of the ePrivacy Directive — and the GDPR require your consent before any cookie that is not strictly necessary is placed on your device. Until you give it, none is placed.
que_son.p3: Rejecting is as easy as accepting: the banner has an “Essential only” button at the same level as the accept button. Closing the banner without choosing does not count as accepting — nothing is enabled and you will be asked again — and your decision is stored for 24 months, after which you are asked once more.

tipos.title: 2. Types of cookies we use
tipos.intro: We classify our cookies into the following categories:

items.purpose: Needed for the site to work and to protect it from automated submissions. They do not require consent.
Remember the language and theme you choose. They are exempt from consent because they are the interface personalisation you asked for yourself, which is why they show as always on in the panel.
items.examples: Preferred language, light or dark theme.

items.purpose: Help us understand how the site is used so we can improve it. They are the only ones that depend on your consent, and they stay denied until you give it.

tabla.title: 3. List of cookies used
tabla.intro: Your choice in the preferences panel is not stored in a cookie but in the browser's local storage (localStorage), which serves the same purpose but is not sent with every request to the server. This is everything that is stored on your device:

rows.name: na:cookie-consent
rows.purpose: Stores which cookies you have accepted and when, so you are not asked on every visit.

rows.name: NEXT_LOCALE
rows.purpose: Stores the language you have chosen.

rows.name: next-auth.session-token
rows.purpose: Keeps you signed in to the private area. Only created if you sign in.

rows.name: Cloudflare Turnstile
rows.duration: For the duration of the check
rows.purpose: Verifies that whoever submits the form is a person. Cloudflare may store technical information on your device while the check lasts.

rows.name: _ga
rows.purpose: Identifier Google Analytics uses to tell visitors apart. Only placed if you accept analytics.

rows.name: _ga_<container>
rows.purpose: Keeps the Google Analytics session state. The suffix is the identifier of our measurement property.

terceros.title: 4. Third-party cookies and services
terceros.intro: These are the third parties involved, what they receive and where to read their policy. Each of them is responsible for its own processing:

list.strong: Google (Google Analytics via Google Tag Manager):
list.rest: only if you accept analytics cookies. The container always loads, but it starts with every consent signal denied, so until you accept it writes no cookies and sends no identifiers. The advertising signals are denied at all times, because there is no advertising tag installed on this site.

present on every public form. It receives your IP address and technical browser data, and may store information on your device while the check lasts. It is essential for the form to work, so it falls under the strictly necessary exemption.

pages with a map request the imagery from its servers, which receive your IP address when serving it. It sets no cookies: it is an image request like any other, but you should know about it because a third party is involved.

terceros.outro: There is no other third party. In particular, there are no social network pixels, no remarketing tags and no advertising cookies of any kind.

gestion.title: 5. How to manage cookies
gestion.manageIntro: You can change your decision — or withdraw it entirely — at any time from the panel, without giving any reason and with the same effort it took to give it:
gestion.browserIntro: You can also control cookies from your browser settings:
gestion.withdrawNote: Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of what was measured while it was given. If you withdraw it, analytics cookies stop being placed; any already on your device can be deleted from your browser settings, as explained below.

Complaints.title: Complaints channel
Complaints.subtitle: A direct, confidential channel for reporting breaches, irregularities or conduct contrary to regulations related to our activity.

queEs.title: What this channel is
queEs.intro: The whistleblowing channel is Imora's internal reporting system: the route for reporting any breach of the rules, irregularity or conduct contrary to professional ethics detected in the course of our activity, in accordance with Spanish Act 2/2023 on the protection of persons who report regulatory breaches.
queEs.p2: The system has been approved by the company's governing body, which has appointed a person responsible for running it with autonomy and independence, and it has a written internal procedure setting out how each report is handled.

quienPuedeUsarlo.title: Who can use it
quienPuedeUsarlo.intro: This channel can be used by anyone with a direct relationship with Imora, including:

list.rest: concierges, controllers, technicians and administrative staff.
homeowner communities, buildings and shopping centres that receive our services.
companies and self-employed professionals who work with Imora.
people who have had or will have an employment relationship with Imora.

queComunicar.title: What can be reported
queComunicar.intro: This channel can be used to report matters such as:

list.rest: infringements of employment, safety or environmental law.
workplace, sexual or discriminatory conduct towards anyone.
serious breaches of what was agreed with a community or building.
personal data processing contrary to data protection regulations.
bribery, undeclared conflicts of interest or misuse of company resources.

comoComunicar.title: How to report it
comoComunicar.intro: You can file your report in writing, through the guided wizard, describing the facts in as much detail as possible: what happened, when, who is involved and whether you have any evidence. You can do so with your name and email, so we can confirm receipt, or tick that you would rather not identify yourself.
comoComunicar.highlight: The identity of the person filing the report and that of any third party mentioned are treated confidentially throughout the process, with access restricted to the staff in charge of handling it. It is not disclosed to the person the report concerns or to anyone outside the procedure.
comoComunicar.verbal: you can report verbally by writing to the system manager's address to ask us to call you, or by requesting a face-to-face meeting: if you ask for one, it is held within seven days. What is discussed is recorded in writing, or by recording if you authorise it, and in both cases you are offered the chance to check, correct and sign it.

garantias.title: Guarantees
garantias.intro: Managing this channel is governed by the following guarantees:

list.rest: the whistleblower's identity is not disclosed to third parties without their express consent, unless disclosure is a legal obligation in the course of a judicial or administrative investigation, in which case they are told beforehand.

no form of retaliation — dismissal, change of duties, exclusion from processes, reputational harm — is tolerated against anyone who reports in good faith, or against those around them. Whoever does so answers for it.
receipt is confirmed within a maximum of 7 calendar days, unless doing so could jeopardise confidentiality.

the investigation and the reply are completed within a maximum of 3 months from acknowledgement of receipt, extendable by a further 3 months in particularly complex cases, with notice of the extension and its reasons.
the person the facts concern is informed and can give their account, with the presumption of innocence and without being told who reported.
every report is entered in a confidential register, made available to the competent authority only on a reasoned request.

canalExterno.title: External channel
canalExterno.intro: You are not required to use this channel before any other, nor to exhaust it. You may go directly to:

list.rest: the external channel provided for by Act 2/2023, which can be used with or without a prior internal report, and anonymously.
the autonomous communities that have set up their own whistleblower protection authority are competent within their territory.
where the breach affects Union law.

canalExterno.outro: Using the external channel does not cost you any of the protections under Act 2/2023. If the facts could constitute a criminal offence, the report is forwarded to the public prosecutor.

datos.title: Data protection
datos.intro: Processing of this channel's data is governed by Act 2/2023 and by the GDPR, with these particularities:

list.rest: compliance with a legal obligation (art. 6(1)(c) GDPR), not your consent. That is why it is not requested.
only data strictly necessary for the investigation is processed. Anything else is deleted immediately, and data supplied by mistake is not kept.
data is kept only for as long as strictly necessary. If no investigation has been opened three months after receipt, the report is deleted and only an anonymised entry remains in the register.
only the person responsible for the system and, where applicable, whoever conducts the investigation have access; and the head of human resources or legal counsel where measures need to be taken.

you may exercise the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection on the terms of the privacy policy, with the limitation that they do not give access to the whistleblower's identity.

contacto.responsible: Manager of the internal reporting system
contacto.intro: For any question about how the channel works, or to request a face-to-face meeting:
